name: SAUDI ARABIA
lead: Saudi Arabia is a huge desert kingdom on the Arabian Peninsula. Mecca and Medina, Islam's holiest cities, are here. Millions of pilgrims visit every year. Under the dunes lie some of the world's greatest oil reserves.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Most of Saudi Arabia is high, flat land of sand and gravel. The Rub' al Khali, or Empty Quarter, is the world's largest continuous sand desert. Its dunes reach 250 metres.
Mountains called the Hejaz and Asir run along the west. Rain falls there. Coral reefs line the Red Sea coast. The Persian Gulf lies in the east.
animals: The dromedary, a one-humped camel, can go a week without water. Arabian oryx once died out in the wild. People bred them and set them free.
Saudis have trained falcons for 2,000 years. Peregrine and Saker falcons are prized partners. The rare Arabian leopard lives in the Asir highlands.
culture: Muslims here pray five times a day. During Ramadan, they do not eat from sunrise to sunset. At Eid, families feast on lamb, kabsa rice and sweet dates.
Guests get qahwa, a cardamom coffee, and dates. Many people wear a white thobe or a black abaya. City clothes are modern too.
history: Bedouin tribes crossed these deserts for thousands of years. Mecca was a trading town before Islam. The Prophet Muhammad was born there around 570 CE.
In 1932, King Abdulaziz ibn Saud joined warring tribes into one kingdom. Soon after, huge oil fields were found. A desert land became a world power.
wows: The Rub' al Khali could swallow all of France with room left over.
Saudi Arabia has no permanent rivers, not a single one.
The Hajj brings nearly 2 million people to Mecca in one week.
Saudi Arabia holds roughly 17% of the world's proven oil reserves.
Al-Ula's Hegra has Nabataean rock tombs carved over 2,000 years ago.
NEOM's 'The Line' is a planned 170 km city, with no roads or cars.
The Arabian oryx may have inspired the unicorn legend.

myths.myth: Camels store water in their humps
myths.fact: A hump holds fat, not water. The fat gives energy when food is scarce.

myths.myth: Non-Muslims can never visit Saudi Arabia
myths.fact: Tourist visas began in 2019. Non-Muslims can visit ruins, deserts and beaches. Only Mecca and Medina's holy centre are closed to them.
